legend: Chloe wants to test her sorting skills. She has n$$$n$$$ cards with distinct integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ written on them. She asks her little brother Connor to first blindfold her and then arrange all cards in a row in some order. Positions of cards are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ from left to right.

Chloe doesn't know the order of the cards, but she wants to sort them, so that the leftmost card has number 1$$$1$$$ and the rightmost card has number n$$$n$$$ on it. Formally, for each i$$$i$$$ she wants the card on position i$$$i$$$ to have number i$$$i$$$ on it. To achieve the goal, Chloe can ask Connor to do one or more operations.

Each operation can be denoted by two integers posi$$$pos_i$$$ and posj$$$pos_j$$$ (1≤posi<posj≤n$$$1 \le pos_i  \lt  pos_j \le n$$$). Connor looks at the cards on positions posi$$$pos_i$$$ and posj$$$pos_j$$$, and if the card on position posi$$$pos_i$$$ has a bigger number than the card on position posj$$$pos_j$$$, he swaps them. Otherwise, he does nothing. Connor also tells Chloe if he swapped the cards or not.
To make the game more interesting, after every 2n$$$2n$$$ operations Connor chooses two distinct cards uniformly at random and swaps them without telling anything to Chloe.
If after some of Chloe's operations all cards become sorted, Chloe wins. Help Chloe to sort all cards using at most 10 000$$$10\ 000$$$ operations.
Your program should start by reading a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤50$$$2 \le n \le 50$$$) — the number of cards.

Your program can ask to do the specified operation one or more times. To do the operation, your program should print its description formatted as "posi$$$pos_i$$$ posj$$$pos_j$$$" — two distinct numbers denoting the positions of cards (1≤posi<posj≤n$$$1 \le pos_i  \lt  pos_j \le n$$$). Remember to flush the output after printing each operation description. Then your program should read the outcome of the operation — it will be a single word SWAPPED if the cards were swapped, or a single word STAYED if nothing changed.

If instead of an operation outcome your program receives a single word WIN, it means that the cards have become sorted. Your program should terminate silently after that, it is not allowed to output any extra operations.

After every 2n$$$2n$$$ operations two distinct cards are chosen randomly and swapped without telling anything to your program. Each pair of cards has equal probability to be chosen. This swap is not counted as an operation.
note: Initial card ordering in the example was 3$$$3$$$ 1$$$1$$$ 2$$$2$$$ (that is, the card on position 1$$$1$$$ had number 3$$$3$$$ on it, the card on position 2$$$2$$$ had number 1$$$1$$$, and the card on position 3$$$3$$$ had number 2$$$2$$$).

legend.ai: Chloe 想检验自己的排序技巧。她有 n$$$n$$$ 张卡片，上面写着 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 这 n 个互不相同的整数。她让弟弟 Connor 先蒙住她的眼睛，然后把所有卡片按某种顺序排成一行。卡片的位置从左到右编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$。
Chloe 不知道卡片的顺序，但她想要排序，使得最左边的卡片数字为 1$$$1$$$，最右边的卡片数字为 n$$$n$$$。形式化地说，对于每个 i$$$i$$$，她希望位置 i$$$i$$$ 上的卡片数字为 i$$$i$$$。为了达到目标，Chloe 可以要求 Connor 执行一次或多次操作。

每次操作可以用两个整数 posi$$$pos_i$$$ 和 posj$$$pos_j$$$ 表示(1≤posi<posj≤n$$$1 \le pos_i  \lt  pos_j \le n$$$)。Connor 查看位置 posi$$$pos_i$$$ 和 posj$$$pos_j$$$ 上的卡片，如果位置 posi$$$pos_i$$$ 上的卡片数字大于位置 posj$$$pos_j$$$ 上的卡片数字，就交换它们；否则不操作。Connor 还会告诉 Chloe 他是否交换了卡片。
为了让游戏更有趣，每经过 2n$$$2n$$$ 次操作后，Connor 会均匀随机地选择两张不同的卡片并交换它们，且不告诉 Chloe 任何信息。
如果在 Chloe 的某次操作之后所有卡片都排好序了，Chloe 就赢了。帮助 Chloe 使用至多 10 000$$$10\ 000$$$ 次操作将所有卡片排好序。
你的程序应首先读入一个整数 n$$$n$$$(2≤n≤50$$$2 \le n \le 50$$$)——卡片的数量。

你的程序可以请求执行指定操作一次或多次。若要执行该操作，你的程序应将其描述按照 "posi$$$pos_i$$$ posj$$$pos_j$$$" 的格式输出——两个不同的数字，表示卡片的位置(1≤posi<posj≤n$$$1 \le pos_i  \lt  pos_j \le n$$$)。记得每次输出操作描述后刷新输出。然后你的程序应读入操作结果——如果卡片被交换，结果将是单词 SWAPPED；如果没有发生变化，结果将是单词 STAYED。
如果你的程序接收到的不是操作结果而是单词 WIN，这意味着卡片已经排好序。此后你的程序应静默终止，不允许再输出任何额外操作。
每进行 2n$$$2n$$$ 次操作后，会随机选择两张不同的卡片并交换它们，而不会将任何信息告知你的程序。每一对卡片被选中的概率相等。此次交换不计入操作次数。
